課程簡介Course Description

New Media Practicum is a hands-on, production-oriented course designed to familiarize students with contemporary video production workflows, with particular emphasis on the practical application of virtual studio technologies. The course guides students through the end-to-end process of planning, producing, and refining short-form and interview-based video programs by integrating on-location shooting with virtual studio environments. Throughout the semester, students work in small production teams to identify a project theme related to innovative technologies, digital media, or communication technologies, and develop a series of video outputs in different program formats. Emphasis is placed on studio setup, camera operation, lighting design, real-time compositing, interview planning, and on-camera performance, as well as role coordination within a production team. Through iterative hands-on practice and collaborative production cycles, students strengthen their technical proficiency, workflow management, and applied storytelling skills, enabling them to translate conceptual ideas into coherent, professional-quality audiovisual content suitable for contemporary digital media platforms. To help students master virtual studio operations, we have invited Production Manager Peter Su(蘇偉智) and Multimedia Engineer Jamie Lin(林士堯) from Forever Tech as our guest instructor to co-teach this course; they will provide six weeks of on-site technical guidance and hands-on support at the studio.

Conduct and record professional interviews by integrating effective questioning strategies, on-camera performance, and virtual studio coordination.

Collaborate in small production teams to manage roles, workflows, and problem-solving processes in a studio-based production setting.

Translate selected topics into coherent audiovisual narratives by combining technical execution with creative storytelling strategies.

Critically evaluate produced media works by reflecting on technical quality, narrative effectiveness, and production decisions.

Written Report (10%)

Student performance in this course is evaluated through a combination of participation, production outcomes, technical practice, and written reflection. Assessment places particular emphasis on the development of informative video programs centered on topics related to technology, innovation, digital media, and communication, in alignment with the core educational focus of GCIT. Working in groups, students are required to design and produce three video programs based on a selected topic, incorporating both field video shooting outside the classroom and virtual studio–based production. As part of the production process, students will plan and conduct in-studio interviews with invited guests or experts who can meaningfully represent the core ideas of the chosen topic, while collaboratively operating the virtual studio environment. Accordingly, the quality of video production, effectiveness of interview planning and execution, proficiency in virtual studio operation, and engagement in field shooting activities all contribute significantly to the final grade, alongside participation, virtual studio practice, and a written final report that reflects on feedback and learning outcomes.

課程資料Course Details

課程簡介Course Description

Design Thinking for Innovative Talent and Teams in the AI Era

— Build your purposeful career and abundant life

📌 Important Notice Before the First Class

Students who wish to take this course should carefully read the description and policies below, and complete the registration form.

Mandatory Attendance: You must attend the first class (9am Sep. 8, 2026) to be considered a candidate for enrollment.

Pre-registration: You must complete the [registration form](https://reurl.cc/KEQN0y) before coming to the first class.

Course Format: This is a highly interactive course featuring extensive teamwork and collaborative activities. Full engagement and active participation are expected throughout each session.

Class Capacity: : The standard enrollment limit is 25 students (for credit). An additional 5 slots are available for exchange students and visiting scholars.

Enrollment Notification: 

Priority decision (1st tier): Before Sep. 5th

	Early decision (2nd tier): Before Sep. 8th

	Final admission decision: within 24 hours after the first class

🌟 Testimonials

"It’s very satisfying knowing that I am not alone in this journey. I have a group to share my daily achievements and support each other... It feels like life consultation; each class allows us to reflect on our path more and more. Thanks for this amazing journey!!"

"Thank you for all the support and guidance throughout the course! I’ve really appreciated the way you’ve made the material engaging and accessible... Looking forward to seeing all of you next week!!"

"I’m not usually comfortable speaking in public or talking to new people, but everyone in this class was so welcoming and warm. The vibes are great, allowing me to make new friends and practice speaking up without pressure. Thanks a lot for this insightful class!!"

— Inspiring feedback from NCCU DT Class of 2024–2025!

🌟 Course Introduction

In an AI era defined by rapid change and ambiguity, this course equips advanced undergraduate and graduate students with Design Thinking (DT) principles and innovative problem-solving tools to build effective teams and thrive in both life and career.

To avoid the pitfall of learning theory without practice, every single session in this course is divided into a "Two-Half Structure":

The Macro Track (1st half): Master macro-level design methodologies, cross-disciplinary tools, and tech-AI mindsets applicable to corporate and global ecosystems.

The Micro Track (2nd half): Turn the lens inward. You will use your own life as a sandbox for a semester-long Personal Project, executing real-world behavior design experiments.

Our curriculum spans 16 transformative weeks, structured into three golden phases:

Phase 1: DT Fundamentals & Habit-Forming Project (Weeks 1–5): Master classical d.school methodologies while executing a SMART habit-design experiment to optimize your personal energy.

Phase 2: AI-powered DT & Good Life Upgrade (Weeks 6–10): Navigate the digital age. Learn to leverage AI as a high-performance collaborative peer while scaling your habits into a Good Life Project Prototype anchored in Purpose, Achievement, and Enjoyment.

Phase 3: Re-engineering of Life, Career & Resilience (Weeks 11–15): Apply design mindsets to your future career blueprint. Tackle your life priorities, navigate unchangeable limitations, map out alternative pathways, and establish your personal "Life Board of Directors" to bounce back gracefully from setbacks.

🧭 Guidance & Expectations

🧭 For Introverts:

About one-third of our past students identified themselves as introverts before joining. By the end of the semester, every single one of them successfully found their rhythm and navigated the course beautifully. Many were pleasantly surprised by how many genuine friendships they formed along the way!

🧭 For busy students with heavy credit loads or extracurriculars:

"I really appreciate the engaging courses you’ve designed. I never thought I would have this much fun in a college classroom. Thank you!!"

This course is designed to be a space where you can pause, recharge, have fun, and create something inspiring for yourself, your team, and the world. Most students find our sessions to be a rewarding break from their usual academic stress.

🧭 Regarding Attendance (Can I maintain the commitment?):

Last year, 50% of the students maintained near-perfect attendance (100%, or missing only 1 class due to medical reasons). Only 5% struggled to meet the course standards. Please note our attendance policy: 3 absences will trigger a formal warning, and a 4th absence will automatically result in a failing grade (no credit).

🎯 Three Major Takeaways:

DT & Tech Mastery: Master the core mindsets of Design Thinking (e.g., Embrace Ambiguity, Defer Judgment, Bias toward Action) while learning to co-ideate with AI, giving you a distinct competitive edge in the technological era.

Elevated Teamwork Confidence: Foster advanced communication, psychological safety, and leadership skills through hands-on collaboration simulations and peer feedback frameworks.

Life Resilience & Navigation: Reframe life's bottlenecks, map out adaptive alternative pathways, and intentionally design a sustainable future—discovering a beautifully iterated "new version of yourself" along the way.

每周課程進度與作業要求 Course Schedule & Requirements

 

week 1

Course Introduction & Icebreaking

Instructional Objectives

• Familiarize students with course expectations, grading policies, and the interactive dynamic.

• Build early psychological safety and connection among peers.

Content & Activities

• Macro Track: Lecture on the course blueprint, the "Two-Half Structure," and instructional objectives.

• Micro Track: Rapid networking simulation and team formation roles overview.

 

week 2

Phase 1: Empathy & Self-Awareness

Instructional Objectives

• Master foundational empathy map and journey map tools.

• Discover hidden personal needs and energy drains in daily routines.

Content & Activities

• Macro Track: Lecture on user research methodologies, Empathy Maps, Journey Maps, and case studies.

• Micro Track: Launching the Habit-Forming Project by defining personal "Fundamentals" (sleep, movement, energy).

 

week 3

Phase 1: Problem Definition & Root Causes

Instructional Objectives

• Reframe chaotic raw data into actionable "How-Might-We" (HMW) design statements.

• Identify root causes of personal inconsistency rather than surface symptoms.

Content & Activities

• Macro Track: Workshop on 2x2 definition tables, drafting Need Statements, and mastering the art of problem reframing.

• Micro Track: Executing the "6A Self-Awareness Framework" to pinpoint the primary obstacles in personal habits.

 

week 4

Phase 1: Ideation & Trigger Design

Instructional Objectives

• Practice deferring judgment and brainstorming high-volume, unconventional solutions.

• Design environmental triggers and psychological cues to sustain habits without pure willpower.

Content & Activities

• Macro Track: Brainstorming drills focused on "Wild Ideas" and leveraging diverse peer perspectives for creative problem-solving.

• Micro Track: Deconstructing the "7 Core Desires" to creatively design attractive psychological triggers for personal habits.

 

week 5

Phase 1: Prototyping Daily Rituals

Instructional Objectives

• Shift from overthinking to rapid execution (Bias toward Action).

• Build a tangible, visual tracker for personal morning or evening rituals.

Content & Activities

• Macro Track: Hands-on "Six-Thinking-Hats" simulation to systematically evaluate and refine experimental ideas.

• Micro Track: Visualizing an ideal day's ritual as a Minimum Viable Product (MVP) utilizing mindful anchors (Smile, Breathe, Align).

 

week 6

Phase 1: Iteration & Habit 2.0 Launch

Instructional Objectives

• Learn to harvest and synthesize experimental data from feedback loops.

• Formulate a resilient, long-term habit framework based on behavior science.

Content & Activities

• Macro Track: Executing the d.school "Wallet Activity" to master rapid, user-centric feedback loops and testing cycles.

• Micro Track: Finalizing and publishing the 5 core pillars of the individual Habit 2.0 Guidebook.

 

week 7

Phase 2: Tech Mindsets & Attention Economy

Instructional Objectives

• Critically analyze the impact of generative AI and the mechanics of the attention economy.

• Diagnose how digital tools enhance performance versus how they hijack attention.

Content & Activities

• Macro Track: Exploration of AI as a collaborative peer and the psychological impacts of constant digital notifications.

• Micro Track: Auditing personal tech habits and tracking screen-time triggers utilizing the Internal Family Systems (IFS) "Thoughts are Clouds" concept.

 

week 8

Phase 2: Core Self & Reclaiming Attention

Instructional Objectives

• Master info-architecture and data-synthesis using advanced prompting mindsets.

• Design structural boundaries to protect mental workspace and emotional energy.

Content & Activities

• Macro Track: Practice prompting as a tool for structuring information and clarifying core intent (The "Lead-from-Within" mindset).

• Micro Track: Establishing personalized digital boundaries and building an emotional fortress against notification anxiety.

 

week 9

Phase 2: Human-AI Collaboration

Instructional Objectives

• Evaluate human-AI partnerships through the lens of Self-Determination Theory.

• Leverage generative AI to break team groupthink and solve bottlenecked problems.

Content & Activities

• Macro Track: Deep dive into Self-Determination Theory (Autonomy, Competence, Relatedness) within the context of automated technology.

• Micro Track: Using AI as a personalized coaching partner to analyze and optimize project hurdles without losing human agency.

 

week 10

Phase 2: Shaping the Good Life Blueprint

Instructional Objectives

• Transition from micro-habits to macro life design across Purpose, Achievement, and Enjoyment.

• Sketch the initial vision and milestone markers for a short-term life project.

Content & Activities

• Macro Track: Deconstructing the "Happiness Triangle" and mapping personal alignment with Ikigai principles.

• Micro Track: Mapping out the 5 Gold Elements of the Good Life Project Prototype via a structured mind map.

 

week 11

Phase 2: Tech Audit & Constructive Feedback

Instructional Objectives

• Master rapid digital prototyping using integrated tools.

• Practice d.school feedback frameworks to refine project frameworks with peers.

Content & Activities

• Macro Track: Strategic breakdown of tech-team roles (Hacker, Goal-Getter, Visionary) and digital prototyping workflows

.• Micro Track: Conducting a comprehensive Tech Audit for the Good Life blueprint and practicing the "i like, i wish, i wonder" peer-review matrix.

 

week 12

Phase 3: The Well-being Triangle

Instructional Objectives

• Audit the dynamic tension between external career achievements and internal psychological health.

• Formulate immediate interventions to correct lifestyle imbalances.

Content & Activities

• Macro Track: Interactive debate on the conflicts within the Well-being Triangle (Life Priorities, Career Focus & Resilience)

.• Micro Track: Striking a radical balance in individual project timelines to actively protect personal mental well-being.

 

week 13

Phase 3: Dynamic Reframing & Constraints

Instructional Objectives

• Distinguish between structural "Gravity Problems" and solvable design challenges.

• Reframe unchangeable realities into creative boundaries for career pivot options.

Content & Activities

• Macro Track: Introducing the "Three Arrows for Decision Making" and categorizing career/life constraints.

• Micro Track: Mapping out Alternative Pathways (Plan B & C) for individual projects to successfully bypass major bottlenecks.

 

week 14

Phase 3: Failure Immunity & Self-Compassion

Instructional Objectives

• Deconstruct Impostor Syndrome and high-achievement anxiety

• Cultivate resilience by treating setbacks as objective pivot data rather than personal definitions.

Content & Activities

• Macro Track: Interactive breakdown of the Five Building Blocks of Self-Esteem, Shame Deconstruction, and Self-Compassion practices.

• Micro Track: Authoring a personalized "Good Life Failure Resume" to systematically wire an internal bounce-back mechanism.

 

week 15

Phase 3: Ecosystems & Personal Board

Instructional Objectives

• Move away from the "lone wolf" mentality to map out strategic stakeholder networks.

• Practice approaching high-profile mentors using tactical networking frameworks.

Content & Activities

• Macro Track: Formulating stakeholder maps and applying the "Link, Learn, Leverage" framework to engage high-value networks.

• Micro Track: Finalizing the individual "Board of Directors" blueprint and initiating outreach for alternative project pathways.

 

week 16

Phase 3: Final Launch, Storytelling & Gratitude

Instructional Objectives

• Synthesize 15 weeks of personal data into a compelling, transformative narrative

.• Formally commit to an autonomous, long-term action experiment beyond campus boundaries.

Content & Activities

• Macro Track: Master storytelling techniques to present the evolution of the self and leveraging psychological capital (HOPE /HERO).

• Micro Track: The New Version of Self Launch Ceremony, integrated with mindfulness gratitude rituals

***This is an intensive course (10/19~12/21, every Monday at 17:10~19:00).

Classroom: Room 270106, North Wing, General Building***

課程簡介Course Description

The course provides a comprehensive examination on major security issues in Asia-Pacific. The course begins with a broad overview of security environment in the region and is followed by discussions of major security issues.                                 0：無關聯，課程內容、活動及評量均未涉及。

                                2：低度關聯，少數單元或活動涉及，但非主要教學內容。

                                3：中度關聯，明確納入部分教學活動、作業或評量。

                                4：高度關聯，為重要學習內容，融入多數教學活動或評量。

                                0：No relevance: The course content, learning activities, and assessments do not address this competency.

                                1：Very low relevance: The competency is only briefly mentioned in class, with no related learning activities.

                                2：Low relevance: The competency is addressed in a small number of units or activities but is not a major component of the course.

                                3：Moderate relevance: The competency is explicitly incorporated into some learning activities, assignments, or assessments.

                                4：High relevance: The competency is an important learning component and is integrated into most learning activities or assessments.

                                5：Core relevance: The competency is a core learning objective of the course and is addressed through systematic instruction and assessment.

能力A：教授學生運用 AI 學習的能力  Competency A: Teaching Students to Use AI for Learning

0  

本課程培養學生依專業或學習需求，理解、選用及運用AI工具，進行資訊整理、資料產出、提問與自主學習的程度。
This course develops students'ability to understand, select, and use AI tools according to their disciplinary or learning needs for information organization, data or content generation, inquiry, and self-directed learning.

能力B：教授學生負責任使用 AI 的能力  Competency B: Teaching Students to Use AI Responsibly

0  

本課程培養學生遵循學術誠信、智慧財產權、個人資料及相關倫理規範，並辨識AI偏誤、錯誤資訊與資安風險的程度。
This course develops students’ ability to comply with academic integrity, intellectual property, personal data protection, and relevant ethical requirements, as well as to identify AI bias, misinformation, and cybersecurity risks.

能力C：教授學生運用AI解決問題的能力  Competency C: Teaching Students to Use AI for Problem-Solving

0  

本課程培養學生運用AI分析問題、整合專業知識、優化流程，並透過人機協作提出、驗證及修正解決方案的程度。
This course develops students’ ability to use AI to analyze problems, integrate disciplinary knowledge, optimize processes, and propose, validate, and refine solutions through human–AI collaboration.

能力D：教授學生AI無法取代的能力  Competency D: Developing Human-Centered Competencies That AI Cannot Replace

0  

本課程培養學生自主判斷、承擔責任、溝通協作、同理關懷、多元思考及創意實踐等以人為本能力的程度。
This course develops students’ human-centered competencies, including independent judgment, accountability, communication and collaboration, empathy and care, diverse perspectives, and creative practice.
